newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian actress on drug charges brought home.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian actress on drug charges brought home.

text.p: An Indonesian television actress arrested on the run in the United States after being accused of possession of ecstasy pills has been brought home under police escort, the official Antara news agency said on Sunday.

"At this moment I do not have many comments, I am submitting everything to Him above (God) and hope it will be quickly concluded," the actress Zarmina was quoted as telling reporters while earlier in transit on the holiday of Bali.
Antara said Zarima, 24, was later whisked away under police escort from Jakarta's Sukarno-Hatta International Airport after arriving on a Garuda Indonesia flight from Los Angeles.

She was initially detained in August after police said they found 29,667 pills of the designer drug ecstasy in her home but the actress, who had small roles in several local television serials, escaped after asking if she could go home for a bath.

U.S. police detained Zarima on November 4 in Houston, Texas on immigration charges. She had travelled there from Indonesia via Singapore and Malaysia after eluding police for a number of weeks in Indonesia. Indonesia had cancelled her passport.
Indonesia and the United States have no extradition treaty, but Zarima agreed to return to Indonesia under police escort and in the company of her lawyer.
Indonesia's Attorney-General Singgih had pledged to ensure Zarima receives heavy punishment for escaping from custody.

The high-profile case was a major embarrassment for authorities, coming after the May escape from prison of businessman Eddy Tansil who was serving a 20-year term for his role in a high-profile banking scandal.
